Republic of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT A. Francisco Gold Condominium II Bldg, EDSA corner Mapagmahal St., Diliman, Quezon City LEGAL SERVICE DILG OPINION NO. 59 S. 2010 26 May 2010 VICE-MAYOR JESUS C. GONZALES Sta. Ana, Pampanga Dear Vice-Mayor Gonzales: This has reference to your earlier letter asking this Department's legal opinion on the following issues: I) Would it no t be legal, va lid, proper an d judicious to allow the .CP' placer who incidentally is Mr. Vergel Mallari to fill up the vacant position to be vacated by Ms. LapuzP e) Since Ms. Lap uz was fo un d to be no t fit to be a candidate neither to be elected as sangguniang bayan member of Sta. Ana, what will happen now to all the compensation, benefits, allowances and other emoluments that she received from the Municipality.' As culled from the documents submitted to this Department, you previously filed before the Commission on Elections (COMELEC) a Petition to Disqualify Erlinda L. Lapuz as a candidate for the position of Sangguniang Bayan Member in Sta. Ana, Pampanga. During the pendency of your Petition, Ms. Lapuz was elected as one of the eight (8) Sangguniang Bayan Members of Sta. Ana in 2004 and 2007 local elections. On 11 June 2009, the COMELEC (En Banc) issued a Writ of Execution ordering Ms. Lapuz to vacate the position as Sangguniang Bayan Member of Sta. Ana, Pampanga and to cease and desist from performing the functions thereof. Hence, your queries. In reply to your first query, please be informed that Mr. Vergel Mallari, being the 9Ün placer, cannot, as such, be allowed to fill up the position vacated by Ms. Lapuz. Nowhere can we find in pertinent laws or even in jurisprudence that in case of vacancy, permanent or temporary, in the Sangguniang Bayan, the 9th placer in the election shall automatically fill up the position vacated by the incumbent. In fact, in many jurisprudence decided by the Supreme Court, said Court maintained on the contrary, that is, the non-proclamation of the 9Ün placer simply means that he lost in the election. Unfortunately, you were not able to mention in your letter the specific ranking of Ms. Lapuz in the Sangguniang Bayan. Be that as it may, if she was not the eighth ranking sangguniang bayan member, then the rule on automatic

-2- succession provided under Section 44 of the Local Government Code of 1991 (RA 7160) shall first be applied. Thereafter, the eighth place vacancy in the sangguniang bayan shall be filled up by appointment to be issued by the Governor pursuant to Section 45 (a) (2) and (b) of the Code. Section 45 (a)(2) and (b) of the Code prove and we quote: "SECTION 45. Permanent Vacancies in the Sanggunian.— (a) Permanent vacancies in the sanggunian where automatic successions provided above do not apply shall be filled by appointment in the following manner: (2) The governor, in the case of the sangguniang panlungsod of component cities and the sangguniang bayan; (b) Except for the sangguniang barangay, only the nominee of the political party under which the sanggunian concerned had been elected and whose elevation to the position next higher in rank created the last vacancy in the sanggunian shall be appointed in the manner hereinabove provided. The appointee shall come from the same political party as that of the sanggunian member who caused the vacancy and shall serve the unexpired term of the vacant office. In the appointment herein mentioned, a nomination and a certificate of membership of the appointee from the highest official Of the political party concerned are conditions sine qua non, and any appointment without such nomination and certification shall be null and void ab initio and shall be a ground for administrative action against the official responsible therefor. xxx xxx If Ms. Lapuz was the eighth ranking sangguniang bayan member, then the vacancy shall be filled up in accordance with Section 45 (a)(2) and (b). While as explained above, Mr. Mallari, being the 9Ün placer, cannot, as such, be allowed to fill up the position vacated by Ms. Lapuz, if he belongs to the same political party where Ms. Lapuz belonged, he may qualify as an appointee to fill up the eighth ranking, provided however that the conditions sine qua non mentioned under Section 45 (b) of the Code are also complied with. Anent your second query, the Municipality of Sta. Ana may no longer recover from Ms. Lapuz, after her disqualification, the latter's compensation, benefits, allowances and other emoluments that she received prior to her disqualification. Please be informed that prior to Ms. Lapuz's disqualification, she can be properly considered as a de facto officer. A de facto officer is defined by the Supreme Court in the case of Torres vs. Ribo, 81 PHIL 44, as one who has the reputation of being the officer that he assumed to be, and yet is not a good officer in point of law. He must have acted as officer for such length of time, under color of title and under such

-3- circumstances of reputation or acquiescence by the public and public authorities, as to afford a presumption of election or appointment, and induce people, without inquiry, and relying on the supposition that he is the officer he assumes to be, to submit to or invoke his action. Let it be noted that Ms. Lapuz, by the proper authority, was sworn to, allowed to assume as sangguniang bayan member, and is deemed to be rightfully in such office until the COMELEC declared her disqualification from office. Such being the case, she was legally entitled to the compensation, emoluments and allowances legally provided for the position until the declaration of her disqualification. We hope that we have addressed your concern accordingly. Very truly yours, BY AUTHORITY OF THE SECRETARY: .DO EIV ATTY. JES Director III Copy furnished: Director Renato L. Brion DILG-Region Ill San Fernando City The MLGOO Sta. Ana, Pampanga Ls/17
